text:
Amal: Heads up — our weekly triage (Weds 09:00 PT) is clashing with several APAC folks again. After the calendar org migration the recurring series is still showing the old Zoom link, so people are joining the wrong meeting. Can we decide quickly: 1) rotate time (alternate weeks for APAC-friendly slot), 2) keep current time and do async notes for APAC, or 3) recreate the series with the new Zoom link and keep the time? I can run a quick poll (Doodle/Google). Thoughts?

Kevin: I'm leaning toward recreating the series with the new Zoom and keeping the time for now. Note: Google Calendar's "Find a time" + adding conferencing for the new organizer fixes availability view for most folks. Also remember to check "send update to all attendees" so clients get the new link.

Tara: FYI this is a known weirdness — when the event organizer account changes the conferencing metadata on a recurring event doesn't always propagate. Some clients (Outlook) keep the cached link. Workaround I use: create a new recurring series under the new organizer, copy the guest list and description, then cancel the old series after confirming people see the new one.

Brian: I'm +1 for rotating every other week. Makes calendar fairness better and avoids losing APAC participation. If we rotate, let's pin a stable agenda doc in the event and keep notes in the same folder so async folks can follow. Also can we use Redwood's shared calendar (eng-ops calendar) so we don't tie it to a single person?

Amal: Good points. If we recreate the series, I can do it, but would like someone to double-check attendee list and recurring exceptions (holidays/timeoffs). I can also publish a 2-week rotation poll — quick options: (A) keep Weds 09:00 PT, (B) alternate Weds 09:00 PT / Thurs 02:00 UTC (APAC), (C) move permanently to 14:00 UTC. Link (mock): https://doodle.com/poll/abc123 — pls vote by EOD.

Kevin: Quick steps if we recreate (copy/paste in case it's useful):
```
1) New organizer creates new recurring event (same recurrence rule).
2) Add Zoom via "Add conferencing" (use new account).
3) Copy description & agenda (include link to pinned doc).
4) Add guests from old series (copy paste emails).
5) Send update.
6) After confirmations, cancel old series and send a cancellation.
```
Also check the "notify guests" checkbox — otherwise clients won't refresh the conferencing info.

Tara: Note about timezone displays: some attendees will see local time with DST offsets differently depending on their calendar client. When you recreate the event, include a short line like: "Local time check: if this looks wrong, reopen event and use \"Find a time\" to confirm." That avoids accidental no-shows during DST changes.

Brian: If we rotate, I can maintain the biweekly roster and update the calendar owner to eng-ops (so no single person is on the hook). We'll also keep the previous meeting notes in the same doc and add a header with week/UTC time.

zoom-bot: notice: new zoom account for eng-platform created 2026-05-01 14:23 UTC. Old account meetings will not auto-update conferencing metadata. Please recreate recurring meetings if you need the new link.

Amal: OK — poll is up, please vote. If poll shows majority for recreation (and not rotation), Tara — can you take point to recreate the series and I will validate the attendee list?

Tara: I can take it. Will recreate today if poll favors recreation. I'll drop a short confirmation message in this thread when done.

Amal: :thumbsup: thanks — appreciate the quick sync. I'll also add the pinned agenda doc link in the new event when it's created.

Kevin: Nice. One more minor tip: for long recurring series with exceptions, sometimes creating a new 1-year series and then duplicating for the next year avoids weird exception propagation.

Tara: noted. I'll do a 1-year series and set a calendar reminder to review after 11 months.

Brian: Thanks all — sounds like a plan.

Amal: Last: if anyone sees double invites after this, reply here and we'll coordinate cancellations so no one is left out.
